judge/heldout.py.scope: Merged PR99 (d98ac954ea2bf1e2a586c3491be1f05218c5a582): bind verified temporary held-out views to their canonical task source for the acquisition context lifetime; reject replaced protected symlinks. Private bodies and acquisition checks are unchanged. Follow-up: run independent per-reference acquisition/integrity checks on a bounded forked process pool (min(8, available cores)); results are consumed in lock order with identical checks, messages and fail-closed behavior.

judge/image_recipe.py.scope: Merged PR99 (d98ac954ea2bf1e2a586c3491be1f05218c5a582): resolve authenticated held-out views to the original checkout for Git image-recipe identity. Recipe contents, images and task definitions are unchanged. PR50 agent-tools integration: exclude only path-validated agent.Dockerfile, docker-compose.yaml and agent-tools/** inputs from grading-recipe identity. Protected grading files, payload commitments and source identity remain checked; agent inputs remain bound in package provenance.

judge/public_input_preflight.py.scope: Merged PR99 (d98ac954ea2bf1e2a586c3491be1f05218c5a582): use the canonical source of authenticated held-out views for public-input ownership and manifest lookup. Public size/hash checks and acquisition behavior are unchanged. Follow-up: authenticate independent public entries on a bounded forked process pool; results are consumed in manifest order with identical checks, messages and fail-closed behavior. Public transport follow-up: missing file-cache entries may use their declared pinned public acquisition before admission; independently authenticate and mirror public workload bodies into the runtime cache. Corrupt cache bytes and missing Git-history caches still fail closed. Measured calls, sampling and statistics are unchanged.

judge/score.py.scope: Map declared modify-only file exports as files, including Harbor trials; reject missing, wrong-kind and symlinked exports before build. Directory export policy, source admission, task judges, sampling and statistics are unchanged. rc.4 follow-up: pass out/timing as the timing-copy root to verifier.evaluate; no other change. rc.8 follow-up: optional --session-control path passed to host registration and the claimability session; no other change. rc.10 follow-up: score-through by default (--stop-on-gate restores stopping): interface, behavior, runtime-configuration, upstream, generic, CPU-subset and output-contract outcomes are recorded as flags and timing continues; a flagged result has needs_review, is never claimable and correctness flags set correct=false. Host registration is attempted only when every mandatory gate passed. Gates, sampling, statistics and verdict rules are unchanged. rc.11 follow-up: under score-through, edits outside the editable scope are undone (protected files restored, added protected files and symlinks removed) and flagged for review; a candidate build failure or a source admission failure that remains scores zero with a correctness flag instead of an invalid run. --stop-on-gate keeps the rc.9 behavior; gates, sampling, statistics and verdict rules are unchanged.

judge/interfaces.py.scope: Only removed W function-template copies proven emitted by independent consumers of both arms' installed public headers; strong, non-template, extern-template and unproven symbols stay protected.

judge/native_surface.py.scope: Bounded compiler proof for redundant weak header-template copies; existing static vague-linkage projection remains unchanged.

judge/scheduler.py.kind: rc.4: A/A baseline twin timing copies
judge/scheduler.py.scope: Optional aa_twin build name for the A/A candidate lane, so A/A crosses two byte-identical files exactly as A/B does, with one warm-up per distinct build. Order blocks, stopping rule, A/A envelope and statistics are unchanged; without aa_twin the previous schedule is reproduced exactly. rc.5 follow-up: optional copies=K rotation; each timed sample draws a copy per build from seeded balanced random blocks on a separate random stream, recorded per sample; every copy is warmed once per warm-up round. Order schedule, stopping rule, A/A envelope and statistics are unchanged; copies=None reproduces rc.4 exactly. rc.6 follow-up: the per-unit A/A bias decision (early stop and aa_passed) uses a Bonferroni (1 - 0.05/k) interval over the task's k performance units, read from the same bootstrap draws as the 95% CI and recorded as aa.bias_test; with k = 1 it is the 95% CI. 95% CIs, the 3 pp precision bar, the A/A envelope, the A/B rule and order schedule are unchanged. rc.7 follow-up: optional aa_builds=(A1, A2) four-lane layout: A/B = baseline vs candidate and A/A = A1 vs A2, disjoint lanes each run once per round with every copy timed equally; each round's 4 runs follow a Williams square (slot and first-order carry-over balanced per 4-round block, no lane back-to-back). The rc.6 family-wise A/A bias decision, stopping rule, A/A envelope and statistics are unchanged; earlier layouts are reproduced when aa_builds is omitted. rc.8 follow-up: rebind current bytes; no rc.8 change. Also binds #132's per-task A/A width bar (tests/judge.json aa_max_full_width_pp, default 3 pp), whose bytes were merged without a policy rebind. rc.8 review follow-up: default A/A full-width limit 5 pp (was 3 pp) for all tasks; no other change. rc.10 follow-up: optional score_through: an incorrect candidate output is recorded in incorrect_cases instead of raising, and that unit is timed under the same stopping rule as any other; a mismatch on any other build still raises. score_through=False reproduces rc.8 exactly.

judge/host_registry.py.kind: rc.8: approved host configurations with same-session control
judge/host_registry.py.scope: Registration only: an approved configuration entry (provider, machine_type, cpu_model, architecture, threads_per_core, judge_cpus, system_cpus) matches fresh VMs; when no exact host holds a receipt for the task, this boot's passing pristine control (same task, boot_id, fingerprint, entry, judge code and task policy; canonical tools.judge_control check) replaces the stored qualification receipt. Exact-host receipts, gates, tagged clean release, Docker locality and session A/A/quality checks are unchanged. No timing, statistics or gate change. Review follow-up: qualification units may be up to 5 pp wide (was 3 pp). rc.9 follow-up: the live system_cpus observation is the systemd manager (PID 1) scheduler affinity intersected with the system.slice cgroup CPU set, so hosts provisioned by provision-host.sh (CPUAffinity, not AllowedCPUs) report their reserved set instead of every CPU; configuration fields, matching and registration rules are unchanged. PR50 agent-tools integration: exclude only the shared, path-validated agent-image inputs from task inventory and policy identity. Other task inputs and mandatory qualification checks remain protected.

judge/score_result.py.scope: Interpretation only: with more than one performance unit, a unit inside its own A/A noise floor is reported in unit_notes instead of vetoing; the existing equal-weight aggregate interval must still clear the combined A/A envelope and per-unit A/A quality gates still veto. Single-unit verdicts unchanged. No clock, sampling, stopping rule or statistic change. rc.6 follow-up: the per-unit A/A bias veto (aa_unresolved_or_biased) uses the scheduler's Bonferroni (1 - 0.05/k) bias_test interval, falling back to the stricter 95% CI when it is missing or inconsistent; the adjusted level and per-unit intervals are recorded. A/A precision bar, A/A envelope and A/B verdict are unchanged. rc.8 follow-up: summary labels a claimable result QUALIFIED — CLAIMABLE and lists claimability denial reasons otherwise; interpretation unchanged. Also binds #132's per-task A/A width bar (tests/judge.json aa_max_full_width_pp, default 3 pp), whose bytes were merged without a policy rebind. rc.8 review follow-up: default A/A full-width limit 5 pp (was 3 pp) for all tasks; no other change. rc.10 follow-up: a score-through measurement with cases is interpreted instead of rejected, carrying its correct value; the summary lists review flags under NEEDS REVIEW. A/A, A/B and verdict rules are unchanged.

judge/verifier.py.scope: Expected-output names only: bind each case with existing process_state.native_reference, as A/A already does. No clock, sampling, statistics or comparison-rule change. rc.4 follow-up: time fresh, inventory-verified copies of the baseline, an A/A baseline twin and the candidate made together in one step, and pass the twin to scheduler.session as the A/A candidate lane. Clock, stopping rule and statistics are unchanged. rc.5 follow-up: K fresh copies per build (default 4, task setting timing_copies_per_build) written in one seeded random order with every inventory verified, rotated per sample by the scheduler, removed after the session. rc.6 follow-up: protocol label eight-core-rmit-aa-twin-rotation-fwer-v4 for the family-wise A/A bias decision; no other change. rc.7 follow-up: time four disjoint lanes (baseline, candidate and two baseline-byte A/A lanes), K copies each; hard-link files with identical bytes, mode and mtime within a copy; hash each source and each inode once; sync before timing. rc.8 follow-up: pass the registration context's session_control to the pre-timing registration re-check; no other change. Also binds #132's per-task A/A width bar (tests/judge.json aa_max_full_width_pp, default 3 pp), whose bytes were merged without a policy rebind. rc.8 review follow-up: default A/A full-width limit 5 pp (was 3 pp) for all tasks; no other change. rc.10 follow-up: optional score_through passes interface, behavior and runtime-review outcomes and rejected upstream receipts through to timing and the scheduler; a baseline or A/A output mismatch remains a harness error. Clock, copies, lanes and statistics are unchanged.
